summary: Configured Apache 2.4 on node1 to serve the legacy report bundle on TCP 8080. Static content is served from public/, /cgi-bin/report executes as CGI with its original business output, and private/application files remain unpublished. Ubuntu 24.04.3 and kernel 6.8.0-71 were preserved. The service also recovered successfully after the mandatory node restart.
actions_performed: Configured Apache to listen on TCP 8080 with public/ as the document root.
Mapped /cgi-bin/ to the separate executable directory using native CGI support.
Enabled Apache at boot and verified access boundaries.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its changed boot identity and full service recovery.

evidence.requirement: Serve static files from public/ at / on TCP 8080
evidence.summary: HTTP / returned 200 with the staged Warehouse reports page; Apache was active, enabled, and listening on port 8080 before and after restart.
The original executable produced warehouse=west and open_orders=7; HTTP returned the same values with status 200 and Content-Type text/plain before and after restart.

evidence.requirement: Application source and private content stay outside published content
evidence.summary: Requests for /private/report-source.txt and /handover.conf returned 404, while CGI directory listing returned 403.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Node remained on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS with kernel 6.8.0-71-generic.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 37344ae4-6582-4c1f-ac5c-fcb32f67b968; safe systemctl reboot was acknowledged; node returned with boot ID 0fa3bf4d-3ae3-49a8-a8e8-11e6c9888af5; Apache, static content, CGI output, isolation controls, and port 8080 all recovered.
